metadata.note: The Detroit, Grand Haven and Milwaukee main line Detroit - Pontiac - Durand - Owosso - Ionia - Grand Rapids - Grand Haven, with its predecessors (Detroit and Pontiac 1839-1855, Detroit and Milwaukee 1855-1878) and its Grand Trunk Western afterlife, drawn from the research report research/branches/detroit_grand_haven_and_milwaukee_railway.txt (2026-11-02) on 2026-11-02. Before this layer the map drew only Detroit - Durand, as part of data/detroit_flint.geojson's gtw-detroit-flint feature. Rule 4 splits share identical geometry: D&P -> D&M at the 1855 consolidation, D&M -> DGH&M at the 1878 reorganisation, DGH&M -> GTW at the 1928 consolidation, GTW -> SEMTA on the commuter trains at 1974. Features break wherever a stretch's opening or closing year differs. Pre-1928 features are drawn on the pre-relocation Royal Oak - Birmingham alignment (OpenHistoricalMap); GTW and commuter features on the present line.
sources: https://www.branchline.uk/jfpdf/michiganrrs2lwrp.pdf (John Fowler, Michigan Railroads (2), route 135 Detroit - Grand Haven (CN): x = Dinsmore 1858, y = Official Guide 1875, e = 1976 Guide / 1979 SEMTA timetable)

https://chicagorailfan.com/stbcgrr.html (Grand Rapids passenger trains, 1942 and 1956 snapshots)

metadata.horsecar_trim: Detroit and Pontiac, Detroit - Royal Oak: horse-drawn from its 1838 opening until the first locomotive (Aug 1838, or 1839 per a second source); the 1838 horse year is trimmed and the line drawn from 1839 (Rule 5). Whether horses still hauled D&P cars on the Detroit city streets after steam began is UNRESOLVED.
metadata.not_yet_sourced: OPEN ENDS / OPEN STARTS - (1) gtw-dghm-detroit-grand-rapids ends 1959, the last year certain on every reading; sources say 'until 1960' and a trains.com snippet implies Durand - Grand Rapids was gone before 27 Mar 1960. (2) gtw-dghm-grand-rapids-grand-haven ends 1955 on secondary sources (Wikipedia coal tipple, marker snippet); the primary-source confirmed year is 1951 (Feb 1952 Official Guide). (3) dm-ferrysburg-grand-haven starts 1875 [OPEN START], the first confirmed year (Fowler 1875 Guide); bridge and depot are dated 1870 only by search summaries. (4) cm-coopersville-marne ends 2022 [OPEN], the latest confirmed year; the railway is believed still to run. OTHER: D&P horse/steam boundary 1838/1839 and horses on Detroit streets; Birmingham opening 1838/1839/1841 and Pontiac 1843/1844/1848 (drawn 1841, 1848 - up to 7 years may be missing); Ionia Aug 1857 vs an 'April 3, 1856' search summary; whether St. Johns was a 1856-57 terminus; 1882-1928 Grand Trunk lease/operation of the DGH&M (an ICC valuation would settle it); commuter operator 1974 vs 1978; Royal Oak - Birmingham relocation 1929 (Fowler) vs 1 Aug 1931 (OHM); 1876-1941 rests on continuity, not a dated timetable; the 1858-c.1870 Dewey Hill terminal leg alignment; individual station years.
metadata.omitted: NOT DRAWN: (a) report block [10], Grand Rapids - Muskegon, GTW trains over the Pennsylvania's ex-GR&I Muskegon branch - not DGH&M track and its start is unknown (trackage rights 1930 from a low-grade source; first confirmed timetable 1942), so it is left for the GTW/PRR research. (b) block [12], the 1878 Detroit - Lansing through coach via Durand over the Chicago & Northeastern - not a DGH&M line. (c) GTW passenger trains over Detroit - Pontiac - Durand AFTER 1959 (the Detroit - Chicago trains via Durand to 30 Apr 1971 and the Detroit - Durand locals 21/56): those are the GTW Chicago route and out of scope for this layer; nothing on the map draws Detroit - Durand 1962-1971 yet. (d) The Michigan Air Line, the Chicago & Grand Trunk Durand - Lansing line, the Toledo, Saginaw & Muskegon (Owosso Jct - Muskegon), the Pontiac, Oxford & Northern and the Cincinnati, Saginaw & Mackinaw - separate GT-controlled companies, not DGH&M property. (e) The Lake Michigan car ferries and steamers from Grand Haven and Muskegon - boats. (f) Freight-only years: Grand Haven trackage 1956-1975, Durand - Grand Rapids - Coopersville after 1959 (Rule 1).

properties.geometry_quality: 13.0 mi drawn Detroit (Brush Street) - Royal Oak (1st); Fowler's mileage for Royal Oak (1st) was not read, the D&P whole is 25.9 mi (Fowler) against 25.9 mi drawn to Pontiac. Traced on OpenHistoricalMap; no straight-line leg except a 0.09 mi join at Royal Oak. LATER-TERMINAL: the D&P's 1838-51 Detroit terminals (Dequindre/Jefferson, then Gratiot/Farmer) are not drawn; the line runs to the Brush Street terminal of 1852, later than every year of this feature. Royal Oak (1st) station is located only by projecting the town centre onto the line (265 m off).

segments.note: Opened to Royal Oak in 1838 (19 May per michiganrailroads' 1838 timeline; other sources July or autumn 1838) with HORSE-drawn cars; the first locomotive was bought in August 1838 (MRR-1838) or the line stayed horse-drawn 'until the following year' (second source), and a newspaper advertisement for two daily steam trains from 1 June 1839 is reported. The 1838 horse year is TRIMMED under Rule 5 and the segment drawn from 1839, the first year steam working is certain. UNRESOLVED: a 1913 reminiscence (michiganrailroads' D&P page) speaks of 'the car line operated by horses running into Detroit' - it is not known whether horses still hauled cars on the Detroit city streets after steam began, or whether the strap-rail road ever fell back on horses in the 1840s-early 1850s; a Detroit Free Press search 1838-1850 would settle it. Ends 1855 because the D&P was consolidated into the Detroit and Milwaukee that year; service continued under the new company. The D&P's own early Detroit terminals (Dequindre/Jefferson 1838-42, Gratiot/Farmer 1842-51) are not drawn: the line is drawn to the later Brush Street terminal. Headway is an estimate and is NOT sourced (Rule 3).
sources: Segment-level: 1839 start = first certain steam year (MRR-1838 locomotive Aug 1838 vs 'horse-drawn until the following year'; 1838 horse year trimmed, Rule 5); 1855 end = consolidation into the Detroit and Milwaukee (MRR-DM). Headway NOT sourced. (as checked by the research report research/branches/detroit_grand_haven_and_milwaukee_railway.txt (2026-11-02))

Detroit - Pontiac on OpenHistoricalMap's pre-relocation alignment; Pontiac - Fenton on the OSM CN Holly Subdivision (old_railway_operator=GTW). APPROXIMATED: 0.67 mi straight line just south of Birmingham (1st) station, bridging a gap between two OHM Detroit and Pontiac ways ((-83.2056, 42.5382) to (-83.2113, 42.5471)); two further joins of 0.09 mi each at Royal Oak are also straight. OHM dates the switch to the new line 1 Aug 1931; Fowler says 'former route until 1929' - CONFLICT recorded. Every year of this feature precedes both dates, so the old alignment is the right one for it. Detroit end is the 1852-1973 Brush Street terminal.

segments.note: Detroit - Pontiac passed from the Detroit and Pontiac to the Detroit and Milwaukee at the 1855 consolidation (approved by the Legislature 14 Feb 1855). Pontiac - Fentonville opened 3 Oct 1855: 'the cars on this road commenced running from Fentonville', 1,500 passengers the first day to the State Fair (michiganrailroads' D&M chronology). Fowler records Springfield (Andersonville) in Dinsmore's 1858 guide and Drayton Plains, Waterford, Clarkston, Davisburg, Holly and Fenton in the 1875 Official Guide. Ends 1878 because the bankrupt D&M was reorganised as the Detroit, Grand Haven and Milwaukee Railway (completed 9 Nov 1878): a new corporation with the same property and staff, split here per repo precedent. Great Western (Canada) financial control from 1858 and the 1860 receivership/foreclosure did not change who ran the trains (the D&M's own 1869 passenger timetable survives at The Henry Ford). Headway is an estimate and is NOT sourced (Rule 3).
sources: Segment-level: 1855 = consolidation and the 3 Oct 1855 opening to Fentonville (MRR-DM); 1858/1875 station listings (Fowler); 1878 end = DGH&M reorganisation (MRR-DGHM, WP-DGHM). Headway NOT sourced. (as checked by the research report research/branches/detroit_grand_haven_and_milwaukee_railway.txt (2026-11-02))

segments.note: Fenton was the terminus from Oct 1855; the line reached Corunna 20 Jun 1856 ('passenger and freight trains are making regular trips to that point') and Owosso about 25 Jun 1856 (michiganrailroads' D&M chronology; a search summary gives 1 Jul 1856 for Owosso - same year). No separate Linden/Gaines opening was found, so 1856 is both the earliest possible and the confirmed year. Durand did not yet exist: it grew in the 1870s at the crossing with the Chicago & Lake Huron. Ends 1878 because the bankrupt D&M was reorganised as the Detroit, Grand Haven and Milwaukee Railway (completed 9 Nov 1878): a new corporation with the same property and staff, split here per repo precedent. Great Western (Canada) financial control from 1858 and the 1860 receivership/foreclosure did not change who ran the trains (the D&M's own 1869 passenger timetable survives at The Henry Ford). Headway is an estimate and is NOT sourced (Rule 3).

segments.note: The D&M reached Grand Rapids 15 Jun 1858 (michiganrailroads' D&M chronology; its 1858 timeline gives 2 Jul arrival and the first regular passenger train 4 Jul 1858 - same year), Mill Point (Spring Lake) 6 Sep 1858 and its Grand Haven terminus 29 Nov 1858 (line 'opened between Detroit and Grand Haven' 22 Nov 1858 per the 1903 Commissioner's report via michiganrailroads' DGH&M page). That 1858 terminus was on the NORTH bank of the Grand River (a depot-hotel on Dewey Hill with a ferry to the town; search summaries only), so the 1858-1874 line is drawn to Ferrysburg and STOPS there: the Dewey Hill leg's alignment is unknown and is not drawn. The south-bank Grand Haven extension is a separate feature from 1875. Ends 1878 because the bankrupt D&M was reorganised as the Detroit, Grand Haven and Milwaukee Railway (completed 9 Nov 1878): a new corporation with the same property and staff, split here per repo precedent. Great Western (Canada) financial control from 1858 and the 1860 receivership/foreclosure did not change who ran the trains (the D&M's own 1869 passenger timetable survives at The Henry Ford). Lake Michigan car ferries from Grand Haven from 1902 are boats and not drawn. Ends 1928 at consolidation into the Grand Trunk Western; service continued.
